To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incidence of laryngeal carcinoma was 1:100000 per annum.

1) The incidence of laryngeal carcinoma was highest in the 50–75 age group; 2) Most patients were in advanced stages of the disease at presentation; and 3) The majority of the patients had squamous cell carcinoma.
97% of patients with larynx cancer were in the 50 - 75 years age range and 62% had glottic cancers, while 26% had supraglottics and only 2% had subglottics.
